title: 2026-10-22_XMRig_Cryptominer_Investigation_1cd
description: Investigate systems for cryptocurrency mining malware and identify the source of high CPU usage.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The IT department has received reports of unusually high CPU usage on several Linux servers in the network. Initial investigations suggest that one or more systems may be infected with cryptocurrency mining malware. Your task is to investigate these systems, identify the source of the high CPU usage, and determine if any systems have been compromised by cryptocurrency mining malware.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the following systems with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`:
- `miner-host` (192.168.50.5)
- `second-host` (192.168.50.6)

Enter `start` to begin the investigation.
levels.local_content:
You have SSH access to the following systems with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`:
- `miner-host` (192.168.50.5)
- `second-host` (192.168.50.6)

Enter `start` to begin the investigation. Local sandbox access is not required for this scenario.

levels.title: Investigate Suspicious Services
levels.content: Investigate the `miner-host` system and identify any unauthorized or suspicious services running on the host.
levels.solution: Check the status of all services and look for any that appear unusual or out of place. The suspicious service is `sys-monitor`.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Check the status of all services and look for any that appear unusual or out of place.

hints.title: File/Tool/Location Hint
hints.content: Use the `systemctl` command to list all services and their statuses.

hints.title: Methodology Hint
hints.content: Look for services that are not part of the standard system installation or have unusual names.

levels.title: Identify High CPU Process
levels.content: On the `miner-host` system, identify the process responsible for the abnormal CPU or resource utilization.
levels.solution: Use process monitoring tools to identify processes consuming high CPU resources and investigate their properties. The process responsible is `sys-monitor`.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Use process monitoring tools to identify processes consuming high CPU resources and investigate their properties.

hints.title: File/Tool/Location Hint
hints.content: Use the `top` command to list processes and their CPU usage.

hints.title: Methodology Hint
hints.content: Look for processes with unusually high CPU usage that do not correspond to known system processes.

levels.title: Determine Suspicious Outbound Port
levels.content: Determine which network port is used for suspicious outbound communication from the `miner-host` system.
levels.solution: Investigate active network connections and look for any unusual or unexpected outbound connections. The port number used is `3333`.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Investigate active network connections and look for any unusual or unexpected outbound connections.

hints.title: File/Tool/Location Hint
hints.content: Use the `netstat` command to list active network connections.

hints.title: Methodology Hint
hints.content: Look for connections to external IP addresses on non-standard ports.

levels.title: Locate Malicious Executable
levels.content: Locate the executable or file associated with the suspicious activity on the `miner-host` system.
levels.solution: Correlate the suspicious process with files on disk and investigate any unusual or recently modified files. The filename is `/usr/local/sbin/xmrig`.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Correlate the suspicious process with files on disk and investigate any unusual or recently modified files.

hints.title: File/Tool/Location Hint
hints.content: Use the `ls` command to list files in the `/usr/local/sbin/` directory.

hints.title: Methodology Hint
hints.content: Look for files with unusual names or modification times that do not correspond to known system files.

levels.title: Identify Installation Artifact
levels.content: Identify the artifact responsible for installing or deploying the malicious software on the `miner-host` system.
levels.solution: Investigate installation artifacts and determine how the malware was introduced onto the system. The filename is `/tmp/.installer`.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Investigate installation artifacts and determine how the malware was introduced onto the system.

hints.title: File/Tool/Location Hint
hints.content: Use the `ls` command to list files in the `/tmp/` directory.

hints.title: Methodology Hint
hints.content: Look for files with unusual names or modification times that do not correspond to known system files.

levels.title: Identify External Host
levels.content: Determine the external host communicating with the `miner-host` system for suspicious outbound communication.
levels.solution: Analyze network connections and identify the destination IP address of the suspicious communication. The IP address is `185.183.98.46`.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Analyze network connections and identify the destination IP address of the suspicious communication.

hints.title: File/Tool/Location Hint
hints.content: Use the `netstat` command to list active network connections.

hints.title: Methodology Hint
hints.content: Look for connections to external IP addresses that do not correspond to known legitimate services.

levels.content: Identify the external service used by the `miner-host` system for cryptocurrency mining.
levels.solution: Analyze network traffic to identify the mining pool or command-and-control communication. The port number is `3333`.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Analyze network traffic to identify the mining pool or command-and-control communication.

levels.content: Locate the configuration file used by the malicious software on the `miner-host` system.
levels.solution: Investigate malware artifacts to identify stored configuration information. The filename is `/home/cyrano/.config/sys-monitor/config.json`.

levels.solution: Discover hidden or unusual log files left by the malware. The filename is `/var/log/.sys-mon`.

hints.content: Discover hidden or unusual log files left by the malware.

hints.title: Methodology Hint

levels.solution: Identify service-based persistence mechanisms. The service name is `sys-monitor`.

levels.solution: Investigate logs, scripts, or artifacts revealing malware installation activity. The filename is `/home/cyrano/.bash_history`.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Investigate logs, scripts, or artifacts revealing malware installation activity.

levels.title: Collect Forensic Evidence
levels.content: Collect forensic evidence supporting the identified cryptomining activity on the `miner-host` system.
levels.solution: Gather relevant logs, process information, service configuration, persistence artifacts, and network evidence. Use the following command to create a tarball of the evidence: `tar -czvf forensic_evidence.tar.gz /var/log/.sys-mon /home/cyrano/.config/sys-monitor/config.json /home/cyrano/.bash_history`.

hints.content: Gather relevant logs, process information, service configuration, persistence artifacts, and network evidence.

hints.title: File/Tool/Location Hint

hints.title: Methodology Hint

levels.solution: Correlate collected evidence to classify the activity as unauthorized cryptomining or legitimate system behavior. The activity is malicious.

levels.solution: Apply firewall or network controls to contain the malware. The IP address or port number that was blocked is `185.183.98.46:3333`.
